text:
emma: Hey all, FYI ran into a confusing failure when our frontend (pnpm monorepo) imports @redwood/sdk in an edge function: dev build OK, CI fails with "Cannot find module '@redwood/sdk'" and VSCode shows no types.

nikhil: Sounds like a workspace resolution / hoisting issue. Are you consuming the source package or the built dist? Show package.json of the SDK package.

emma: package.json excerpt: `{"name":"@redwood/sdk","version":"0.2.0","main":"dist/index.cjs","module":"dist/index.mjs","types":"dist/index.d.ts","exports":{"import":"./dist/index.mjs","require":"./dist/index.cjs"}}`. We build to dist in CI before packaging.

sara: If the CI builder is running from the monorepo root, pnpm will symlink packages. Many edge bundlers (esbuild/webpack used by deployer) treat symlinked packages as externals unless you set `preserveSymlinks:false` or configure `bundle` to follow symlinks. Which bundler are you running?

emma: Our deploy pipeline uses esbuild via a custom build step. In local testing toggling preserveSymlinks fixed the runtime module-not-found, but VSCode still complained about types pointing to the workspace root instead of dist.

nikhil: Two pragmatic fixes we've used: (1) postbuild copy of package.json into dist (so the manifest resolution matches published package), and (2) add a `typesVersions` fallback in package.json to help tsserver prefer dist types: `"typesVersions":{"*":{"*":["dist/*"]}}`. Annoying but cross-editor reliable.

emma: Tried copying dist/package.json and typesVersions; editor types are fixed. CI edge bundle still occasionally fails when the SDK calls fetch and retries auth; behavior differs between CJS and ESM builds — only ESM build saw Authorization dropped on retry.

sara: Edge runtimes implement Headers/Request differently. Reusing a Request (req.clone()) can be unsafe if body is a stream or Headers are proxy-backed. For retries, use an explicit copy: `new Request(req.url,{method:req.method,headers:new Headers(req.headers),body:await bufferedBody(req)})`. Buffering is important for non-idempotent/stream bodies.

emma: We were streaming JSON bodies and relied on clone(). Switched to buffering for JSON and recreated Request with new Headers and it fixed ESM edge behavior.

tom: Additional nuance: some bundlers rewrite `exports` lookup for symlinked packages and ignore the `types` condition. To be robust publish-side, include `types` in exports and also keep `types` at top-level package.json. Example: `"exports":{"import":{"default":"./dist/index.mjs","types":"./dist/index.d.ts"},"require":{"default":"./dist/index.cjs","types":"./dist/index.d.ts"}}`.

ikhil: For monorepo DX we added a tiny `examples/monorepo` that reproduces pnpm+esbuild+cloudflare config and a CI job that builds that example against the SDK package in workspace. That catches these symlink/exports regressions before they hit production.

emma: Planning to open a small PR to add docs + example + postbuild script to copy package.json into dist. Will also bump the retry helper to always clone headers explicitly.

infra-bot: Created issue https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/issues/524 (monorepo-edge-resolution) and CI preview at https://deploy.preview/monorepo-edge-checks

sara: TL;DR: when using pnpm workspaces + edge runtimes: ensure bundler follows symlinks (preserveSymlinks:false), include dist/package.json to match published layout, add exports/types + typesVersions for TS, and recreate Requests with copied headers and buffered bodies for retries in worker runtimes.

emma: thanks all — will link PR + CI when ready :rocket:
